title: U.S. air travel could take days to recover after FAA’s lifting of rare nationwide ground stop
html:
Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin says ‘zero evidence’ of cyberattack, while high jet-fuel costs mean fewer flights available to travelers seeking to rebook

The Federal Aviation Administration late Friday lifted the rare nationwide ground stop that left thousands of flights delayed or canceled and stranded people across the U.S. and beyond.

The agency issued the ground stop a little before 4 p.m. Eastern, with relief coming some four and a half hours later. The FAA had cited a “communication issue” impacting air-traffic-control centers and “extraordinary circumstances.”
summary: Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin says “zero evidence” of cyberattack, while high jet-fuel costs mean fewer flights available to travelers seeking to rebook.
